subject: Discovery notes & recommended model matrix + fn-call / JSON validation next steps
summary: Post-discovery recap with recommended model choices for NLU/extraction, links to benchmark results and prompt set, and a short fn-call / structured-output validation checklist. Asks: confirm test vectors, agree on POC scope (3 days, 10k tokens/day), provide SOC2 contact for procurement checklist.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@sundialthera.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@sundialthera.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery notes & recommended model matrix + fn-call / JSON validation next steps

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: automate extraction of clinical trial eligibility criteria and return structured JSON for downstream EHR ingest. Accuracy on entity extraction and strict JSON schema compliance are MUSTs.
- Current constraints: 150 token average snippets, bursty overnight processing windows, and strict PII handling (they cannot leave VPC during POC).

Model recommendations (first-pass):
- Redwood-gpt-small-8k (fp16) — fastest latency, reasonable for classification/extraction in the loop (low cost).
- Open-6B-8bit (quant) — stronger on few-shot extraction; good when we need more nuanced structure.
- Redwood-gpt-medium-quantized — best price/perf tradeoff for structured output.

What we will deliver before the POC kickoff:
1) benchmark report (attached) with token-level latency and token-accuracy on your sample set.
2) prompt set v1 (attached .jsonl) and 50 canonical test vectors we recommend you validate against.
3) fn-call / JSON schema validation checklist + a small runner to test retries and malformed-output handling (link below).

Asks for Sundial:
- Confirm the 50 test vectors we should run (we included a suggested list in the attachments).
- SOC2 contact or security reviewer so we can share the minimal audit-level evidence for the POC (logs, isolated instance details).
- Preferred POC window next week (we suggested Tue–Thu; do you have a preference?).

Next steps: I’ll circulate the benchmark PDF and prompt set now; Neha will follow up with the quantization and evaluation plan. Vanessa will scope the fn-call retry policy and JSON validation harness.

Best,
Markus Klein\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference

Attachments: sundial_benchmark_report_v1.pdf (summary, charts), sundial_promptset_v1.jsonl (50 seeds)
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@sundialthera.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery notes & recommended model matrix + fn-call / JSON validation next steps

Thanks Markus — really helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock POC dates: 

1) For the quantized models, do you have a short note on expected precision loss for entity spans? We need to ensure no regression >1.5% F1 on our annotated set.
2) For the fn-call approach: how do you handle partial/invalid JSON returned by the model? Our downstream pipeline will reject on schema fail — ideally we'd like an automated retry + sanitizer pattern.
3) We need the SOC2 contact for a quick questionnaire — can you include their email?

Can we aim for Tue kickoff? Prefer afternoon PT.

—Lydia\Director, AI Integrations\Sundial Therapeutics
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@sundialthera.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery notes & recommended model matrix + fn-call / JSON validation next steps

Hi Lydia — quick answers and concrete artifacts below. (Markus pinged me to lead the eval plan.)

1) Quantization & expected precision: we ran the 50-sample seed set through an 8-bit calibrated quant run and saw mean entity-span F1 drop of ~0.9% for Open-6B-8bit and ~0.6% for Redwood-gpt-medium-quantized vs fp16. Full table is in the attached PDF (sundial_benchmark_report_v1.pdf). We recommend Redwood-gpt-medium-quantized for the POC to stay within your 1.5% threshold.

2) Partial/invalid JSON strategy (fn-call handler):
- Step 1: model attempt returns JSON-like text. We run a strict JSON parse.
- Step 2: on parse error or schema mismatch: sanitizer (simple heuristics: fix trailing commas, replace smart quotes, attempt to close brackets) and re-parse.
- Step 3: if sanitizer fails, automatically re-invoke the model with a focused retry prompt that includes the failed output and the schema (we recommend up to 2 retries).
- Step 4: if still failing, fallback to a simpler extraction model and flag the sample for human review.

We included a CSV (fncall_schema_checks.csv) showing initial pass rates per model and per retry attempt. Early signal: 72% parse success on first attempt with the medium-quantized model; +18% after sanitizer and one retry.

3) SOC2 contact: security-requests@redwood.ai (primary SOC2 pack) — our security lead, Priya Natarajan, will join if you need a live review.

Artifacts we attached / links:
- sundial_benchmark_report_v1.pdf (CPU/GPU latency, token breakdown, F1 by entity type)
- sundial_promptset_v1.jsonl (50 canonical prompts + expected JSON)
- fncall_schema_checks.csv (per-model pass/fail + retry counts)
- Runner + sample harness: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/fncall-json-validation

POC suggestion: 3 business days, 10k tokens/day, run on Redwood Dedicated (isolated pool) — Markus, can you confirm if Sunny (procurement) needs a separate NDA?

Thanks — I can join Tue afternoon PT for kickoff.

-Neha\Research Applied ML\Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@sundialthera.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 12:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery notes & recommended model matrix + fn-call / JSON validation next steps

Lydia / team — short fn-call validation checklist we plan to run during the POC: 

1) Schema conformance run (50 seeds): run parse -> sanitizer -> retry (max 2) -> fallback. Record where fallback triggers.
2) Determinism stress: run same input 5x across both quantized and fp16 versions to surface non-deterministic field ordering.
3) Tool-call integration: verify that function arguments map exactly to schema keys (we will run an automated comparator between model output and expected canonical JSON).
4) Retry policy: 1 auto-sanitizer pass + 1 model retry (focused prompt) before escalating to fallback. We can tune to 2 retries if you prefer.

Please confirm the 50 test vectors in the attached promptset (we highlighted 10 "edge" cases we think will drive the most regressions). If those look good, we will: provision Dedicated POC nodes (isolated), seed the run, and deliver a daily short report.

Also: procurement — if you want to run this inside your VPC, we will ship the private deployment manifest and minimal KMS integration notes (we'll need the security contact).

-Vanessa\Solutions Engineering\Redwood Inference
